note: Taught: the 44th Amendment, 1978 (w.e.f. 20-6-1979) omitted Article 19(1)(f), removing the Right to Property from the Fundamental Rights.

Taught: Article 20(3) forbids compelling an accused person to be a witness against himself, and Article 21 protects personal liberty; the keyed answer is Article 21 and Article 20(3). The case name (Selvi) is not in the chapter's sources, but the articles are taught.
Taught: Article 19(1)(a) gives freedom of speech and expression.
Taught: Article 21 is the Right to Life and Personal Liberty.
Taught: Article 21 protects life and personal liberty.

Taught: Article 19(2)-(6) permit reasonable restrictions imposed by law by 'the State'; Article 12 defines the State to include the Government and Parliament of India, so the keyed answer (Parliament) follows from the chapter.
Taught by elimination: the chapter teaches the full Articles 14-22 list; Equal Pay for Equal Work is not in it (it is in the Directive Principles, Article 39(d), POL-05).
Belongs to POL-02: Fundamental Duties were inserted by the 42nd Amendment, 1976.
Belongs to POL-02: the right to vote is a Constitutional Right under Article 326.
Belongs to POL-04: the protector of Fundamental Rights is the Judiciary, under Article 32.
Belongs to POL-04: Article 24 prohibits the exploitation of children.
Belongs to POL-18: the Finance Commission is Article 280 and the Election Commission is Article 324.

Belongs to POL-16: Articles 20 and 21 cannot be suspended under Article 359 during an Emergency.
Belongs to POL-04: the Supreme Court and High Courts enforce Fundamental Rights under Articles 32 and 226.
